sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Duivendrecht is a village in the municipality of Ouder-Amstel, next to Amsterdam, and its parking policy is shaped by commuters and travellers who park there to avoid Amsterdam's charges. The council adopted the parking tax ordinance for 2026 on 18 December 2025, in force from 1 January 2026, with a single tariff of 5.37 euros an hour, which the table does not tie to named zones, and a post-payment assessment of one hour of tariff plus 60.20 euros [0]. A resident permit costs 24.25 euros per six months, and business, buffer and specific permits 43.20 euros per month [1]. In the Ouder-Amstel part of the Amstel Business Park, paid parking runs Monday to Friday from 09:00 to 18:00, and businesses and residents there can apply for four permit types [2]. The municipality says all of Duivendrecht lies in a blue zone, introduced because visitors to Amsterdam and travellers to Schiphol parked in residential streets, and residents and businesses without private parking can apply for an exemption from the maximum stay, at 48.50 euros each [4]. A decision of 17 November 2021 made a two-hour disc zone, from 08:00 to 20:00 every day, in Kloosterstraat, Clarissenhof, Michaelplein and the Molenbuurt streets, which were the last residential areas of Duivendrecht without one, citing high parking pressure and long-stay parking by people travelling cheaply to Schiphol or avoiding Amsterdam charges [5].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The big development is the station area. A vision commissioned by the Amsterdam Transport Region for the public space at Duivendrecht station says the first homes of De Nieuwe Kern, with a maximum of 6,200 homes, are due from 2028 with lower parking standards, and car traffic at the station would be limited to kiss-and-ride areas on the edges; the page is undated and a secondary source [11]. The province of Noord-Holland's progress report on hubs of May 2026 lists Duivendrecht among stations where it takes part in planning without paying towards construction, and says the new district will change the hub from a transfer station to one where people also start and end journeys [12]. The province decided in autumn 2025 to widen its advice on municipal parking standards for housing, which municipalities still set themselves [13]. On charging, the municipality designated two charging bays at Populierstraat 33 in October 2023 and two at Astronautenweg 34 in a decision published in June 2024, and public charge points are requested through a market party under an agreement with the Amsterdam Metropolitan Region [6][7][8].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Q-Park lists the P+R Stationsplein at Duivendrecht with 137 spaces, a height limit of 3.50 m, round-the-clock access and number-plate recognition; its tariff did not load, so we record no price [9]. A rail-traveller discount applies at the site, and NS says discounted P+R parking costs at most 9 euros a day, for up to three days, though its page does not name Duivendrecht [10]. Amsterdam's own visitor guide lists park-and-ride rates of 6 and 13 euros but does not include Duivendrecht among its sites, so those are regional context [14]. We found no usage statement for the site and no operator beyond Q-Park's page.

Our data cover only 12 days of this park-and-ride, with 137 spaces. Occupancy averaged about 9% on weekdays and 12% at weekends, with a peak of 76% on a Saturday evening, so it is rarely busy, but the series is too short to say more.
